method: Three caption-blind observers (Claude) each saw only the image; a semantic adjudicator (Claude) saw only the contract and their observations, never the image. AI review is not clinical approval.
inspection: Reference-guided edit of the fluid master: strong red raised dome with a highlight, but the incision rendered as a sutured line.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 1 (Claude)
observers.observation:
1. The left side of a person's head, seen from behind and slightly to the side, in profile facing right. The ear, shaved lower scalp with a darker hairline above, cheek, jaw, and neck are visible.

2. A large, rounded, red-to-pink glowing circle sits on the skin directly behind the ear, in the hollow between the ear and the shaved scalp. Inside it, a short horizontal line of small white dashes or stitches runs across the middle, slightly to the left of the ear. The ear itself looks undisturbed. No dressing or worn object is drawn.

3. No text, arrow, label, or symbol.

4. It could be read as a fresh surgical wound with stitches that has become swollen and inflamed, or as a large boil or abscess behind the ear.

Label: Caption-blind observer (Claude), not a clinician.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 2 (Claude)
observers.observation:
1. The back and right side of a person's head, neck, and upper shoulder, drawn from behind and slightly to the right, so the right ear is in profile. Short dark hair on top, buzzed sides.

2. A round, glowing red-pink patch of skin sits directly behind the right ear, over the bone area, roughly the size of the ear itself. It fades softly into the surrounding skin. Inside the patch, about midway down, there is a short horizontal pale line with tiny crosswise ticks, like a closed cut with stitches. Nothing is worn or applied.

3. No text, arrows, labels, or symbols.

4. A worried patient could read the red area as a fresh burn or an infected, oozing wound, or the crosswise ticks as a rash or teeth marks rather than stitches.

Label: Caption-blind observer (Claude), not a clinician.

observers.label: Caption-blind observer 3 (Claude)
observers.observation:
1. The back and side of a person's head, seen from behind and slightly to the left; the right ear, jaw, and cheek are in profile, with short hair on top and a shaved undercut.

2. A round, glowing red-pink swelling sits just behind the ear, over the bone between ear and hairline. Across its middle runs a short horizontal line with tiny cross-marks, like a closed stitched cut. Nothing worn or applied; no bandage.

3. No text, arrows, labels, or symbols.

4. A patient might read it as a fresh red lump, cyst, or boil with a scar, rather than an expected post-surgical swelling.

Label: Caption-blind observer (Claude), not a clinician.

adjudication.label: Semantic adjudicator (Claude)
recovered: redness behind the ear along a scar or incision
missed: some swelling in the same area
forbidden_hits: Observer 2: "A worried patient could read the red area as ... an infected, oozing wound" (open, discharging wound reading)
adjudication.reason: Observer 2 described a flat red-pink patch that fades into the skin with no swelling, so swelling was recovered by only observers 1 and 3, and Observer 2 also reported the red area could be read as an infected, oozing wound.

outcome: rejected: swelling recovered by two of three observers, one read the flush as a flat patch and named an oozing wound as a misreading

clinician_review.note: Song reviews the accepted image against the claim; this receipt is evidence for that review, not a substitute for it.
